note: Stage c3 claims core/1 with core.events and core.grants, plus core-test/1, and declares the clock.file test control. Computed from each fixture's declared features before implementing, and confirmed by a measured run with core.grants declared and nothing implemented (80 pass, 40 fail, 15 unsupported): the 122 supported are every fixture whose features are a subset of {core.events, core.grants}. The 13 unsupported all need core.capabilities, which arrives in c4; five of them declare the execution profile and are permanently out of reach. Two of the 44 fixtures naming core.grants need clock.file: core.grants.test-clock-never-moves-backward and core.events.subscription-ends-at-grant-expiry, which were exactly the two beyond the computed 13 in that measured run. One fixture needs more than its features declare: core.events.visibility-follows-direct-read-authority expects the provider-origin core.capabilities.changed event a restart with a changed capability records, so c3 records the capability snapshot and its change event without claiming core.capabilities.
